turns.text:
## What the data shows

**The $250 vs $70 figures check out.** For Q2 2026 (2026-04-01 to 2026-07-01), using the `net_contribution` metric (job margin less channel spend):
- Channel B: $10,800 job margin − $800 spend = $10,000 net contribution ÷ 40 leads = **$250/lead**
- Channel A: $8,000 job margin − $1,000 spend = $7,000 net contribution ÷ 100 leads = **$70/lead**

Channel B also converts better (18/40 leads won = 45%) than Channel A (20/100 = 20%), and its jobs are worth more ($1,500 avg revenue vs $1,000).

## Why "double it" doesn't follow, on two separate grounds

**1. There's no marginal-return evidence, only an average.** Channel B's spend has been a flat $800/quarter for six straight quarters (`ledger`, kind=`channel_spend`) — it has never once moved. So $250/lead is the average return at $800 of spend; there is no data point anywhere showing what happens to lead volume when B's spend actually changes. Assuming leads (and therefore the $250/lead rate) scale linearly to $1,600 is an assumption, not a finding.

**2. Even if extra leads materialized, there's no one to do the work.** Every Channel B job in Q2 2026 was a **backflow** service line job. Only one active technician is certified as a backflow-tester: Rafa Osei (T3) — the other certified tech, Tomas Bell, left on 2026-02-28. Rafa logged 488.8 of his 520 available hours in Q2 (`tech_utilisation_pct` = 94%), while the other four active techs sat at 3.85% utilization on other work. Per the certification-required-for-service-line scheduling rule, none of that idle capacity can legally absorb backflow work. Doubling B's lead flow with no second certified backflow tech just means more leads sitting unworked or a compliance breach if an uncertified tech is scheduled anyway.

One more flag: Rafa's backflow-tester certification was issued 2024-03-11 — over 12 months ago, so per policy it's due for re-verification against the issuing body before leaning further on his capacity.

## Bottom line

I can't responsibly say the extra $800 "would bring in" $10,000 (the naive doubling of current net contribution) because that number rests on an untested linear-scaling assumption, and it's moot anyway until backflow capacity is fixed. What I'd actually recommend: (a) get Rafa's certification re-verified and get a second tech certified for backflow before pushing more B leads into the pipe, and (b) if you do increase B spend, do it as a smaller test tranche (not a full double) so you can measure the real leads-per-dollar response before committing more.

I'm not taking any action here since this is analysis, not an executable request.

ANSWER: The $250/$70 net-contribution-per-lead figures are correct for Q2 2026, but doubling channel B spend rests on an unproven assumption (spend has never varied so there is no marginal-response data) and hits a hard capacity wall: only one active technician is certified for backflow work (B's entire job mix) and he is already at 94% utilization. Fix backflow-tester capacity and re-verify that overdue certification before scaling B spend; if you do scale, test with a smaller tranche first to learn the real response rather than assuming linear doubling.
